requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The plan and entrance views establish exposed concrete structure, distinct sports bays, passage on the south and seating integrated with planting on the north. Visible wayfinding assigns Shared Way to the through-route and Activity Floor to the sports area. Perspective occlusion is allowed; reversed zoning, concealed or replaced concrete structure, misplaced labels or seating that blocks the route fails.

Read the schedules, dimensions and relevant details against the records: Shared Way and approaches use broom-finished concrete; Service Strip uses brushed concrete and flush steel grating; basketball uses acrylic-coated asphalt; tennis and fitness use wet-pour rubber over concrete. Planters are freestanding precast concrete, 600 mm high, with 450 mm growing medium and internal drip irrigation; seats use timber slats on freestanding steel frames. Basketball mesh is freestanding and 3,000 mm high, and other new fixtures are freestanding and no higher than 3,000 mm above local ground. The transverse drawing retains 1,200 mm square column shafts and centred 2,400 mm foundations; bridge coverage begins at y = 6,000 mm and its underside is z = 6,240 mm above the southwest datum. Relevant information may be distributed across these sheets; contradictory assemblies, structural attachments or dimensions fail.

Read any operating annotations as records: access is daily 06:00–22:00, sports are daily 08:00–21:00, and passage lighting operates from dusk until 22:00. Depicted use must agree: the 10:00 scene permits active sport and crossing, while 21:30 retains lit public passage and inactive sports equipment. These image roles need not print an hours table, but conflicting stated hours, a closed night through-route or active night sport fails.

The three records establish the upstream specifications; use available process or submission sequencing to assess whether they precede applications, without treating filenames as proof. Analysis and presentation state the four correct zone name–area pairs, totalling 1,728 m². Missing or incorrect source values and contradictory presentation values fail; repetition on application images is checked through carry-through and sets.

The one-page analysis states the four zones and their recorded areas, surfaces, shade and allowances: Shared Way/open sky/40 moving users; Service Strip/open sky/2 maintenance staff; Activity Floor/bridge shade from y = 6 m/40 users and spectators; Garden Edge/bridge shade/18 seated users. Its palette contains the three specified species. The plant/material record assigns each species 2 L stock, DF 72, CP 96 and GM 120, six 6 m × 2 m beds with per-bed counts 12/16/20, and the recorded paving, planter, seat and enclosure assemblies. Implementation is ordered South Link, covering Shared Way and Service Strip at 396 m²; Activity Bays, covering Activity Floor at 1,116 m²; Garden Finish, covering Garden Edge at 216 m². Flexible tabulation is acceptable; missing fields, incorrect mappings or phase order fails.

Plan geometry retains the 72 m east–west by 24 m north–south site, uninterrupted southern 4 m clear route, six centred 4 m protection squares at x = 12, 36, 60 m and y = 8, 20 m, and drainage at y = 4.5–4.8 m over the full length. Dimensioned cuts are transverse x = 36 m, longitudinal y = 2 m and fitness transverse x = 67 m. Both transverse drawings label northward 1% slope, minimum 6,000 mm clearance and maximum 3,000 mm fixture height. Show infrastructure intersected by each cut; off-cut features may be referenced instead of falsely sectioned. The fitness cut crosses F1 and P6. Wrong cuts, lost clearances, encroachments or absent labels fail.

Locate B1 at x = 16–32 m, y = 7.5–19.5 m; T1/T2 at x = 40–46/46–52 m, y = 8–18 m; and F1 at x = 64–70 m, y = 8–18 m. Retain one hoop, one table in each tennis envelope, one pull-up station and two stretching rails, with spectators and approaches around the envelopes. Each sheet identifies its plan location and supplies relevant dimensions: primary basketball and route/service interfaces, tennis spectator edge, fitness footing/approach, column shaft/foundation/protection relationship, and timber seating/precast planter junction. Materials match the submitted schedules and protection space remains clear. Drawing style may vary; missing location references, undimensioned interfaces, shifted envelopes or incompatible construction fails.

Masterplan and the three planting sheets legibly carry the site and all three botanical names. The three planting sheets repeat DF 72, CP 96 and GM 120, distributed as 12/16/20 per bed across six 6 m × 2 m beds at y = 22–24 m and x = 4–10, 16–22, 28–34, 40–46, 52–58 and 64–70 m. All four ground sheets retain the four zone name–area pairs. Summer and winter compositions may change seasonal appearance while preserving species, quantities and bed geometry. Surface-lighting shows junctions and planned light locations. Missing records, changed seasonal inventory or displaced beds/lights fails.

Both documents explicitly identify NORTH SPAN, the three full botanical names, their correct DF/CP/GM code mapping and totals 72/96/120, and the six-bed arrangement with each bed measuring 6 m × 2 m. A readable reproduced schedule counts; missing species, code swaps, incorrect totals or conflicting bed dimensions fails.

Each occupied view preserves the planned structure, facilities, beds and lights. The east pair retains camera position, orientation and framing across day/night; the Garden Edge pair does likewise across seasons. Daytime east shows active sports and passage, tennis dusk shows play and spectators at 18:30, and both 21:30 entrance views show illuminated passage with sports at rest. Garden scenes depict occupied seating and planting at 15:00 with summer/winter appearance. People, weather and seasonal foliage may vary; relocated objects, changed paired cameras, missing occupation or incorrect use states fail.

Review the complete 12-second playback. It visits basketball, table-tennis and Garden Edge boundaries during the occupied 18:30 period, including active sports, before moving to illuminated Shared Way passage at 21:30 with sports inactive. Maintain the plan's facility, bed and light locations throughout. Editing and camera path may vary; a missing boundary, reversed temporal progression, wrong duration or inconsistent layout fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Require at least twelve pages and readable repetition of the four zone areas, botanical names and quantities, and implementation phases in source order: South Link 396 m², Activity Bays 1,116 m² and Garden Finish 216 m², with their respective scopes. State daily access 06:00–22:00 and sports 08:00–21:00. Reproduced source tables count when legible; missing facts, incorrect areas, contradictory hours or insufficient pages fails.

Every submitted specification record, drawing sheet and occupied perspective is visibly identifiable in the presentation. Resizing, cropping and recomposition are acceptable when enough readable content remains to verify reuse. An omitted source, replacement design, title-only mention or unreadable thumbnail fails.

Include a readable north arrow, scale bar, boundary dimensions, four sports envelopes, six protection squares and identifiable lighting positions. Repeat the analysis's zone name–area pairs and plant schedule's botanical names. Bands extend across the full site at y = 0–4, 4–5.5, 5.5–21 and 21–24 m. Graphic conventions may vary; missing annotations, displaced bands or contradictory source records fail.

All six perspectives depict one completed layout with matching facility, planting and lighting positions; each specified comparison pair preserves its camera. Occupation, active sport, illuminated passage and seasonal planting appearance agree with each view's stated time and season.
